To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RHA loading influenced the curing and mechanical properties of rubber composites.
the RHA filler loading influenced slightly on the curing characteristics but significantly affected the tensile properties and hardness of the composites, especially the NR-EPR blends.
the rice husk ash could be utilized as an alternative filler in rubber industry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the utilization of RHA as a new filler in rubber composites and the effects of RHA loading on the tensile properties of NR and NR/EPR composites.
the utilization of RHA filler as reinforcing filler in rubber compounding and its effect on curing, morphology and tensile properties.
the utilization of rice husk as a filler for rubber composites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RHA filler was successfully introduced as a new filler in NR composites.
RHA could be used as an ecofriendly and low cost filler for rubber composites.
the RHA filler loading could be introduced into rubber composites to improve the hardness and compression set properties of the compositing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RHA could be a potential filler for NR/EPR blending in rubber compounding.
the RHA loading could be used as a reinforcing filler in NR and NR/EPR composites to improve the tensile properties.
the rice husk ash can be used in rubber compounding as a reinforcing filler in NR/EPR blending to substitute commercial precipitated silica or any commercial fillers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RHA filler can be used as an effective filler in rubber compounding.
RHA can be used to improve the mechanical properties of rubber composites.
RHA can be used as an eco-friendly filler to substitute other commercial filler for rubber compounding application.
